sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Package list with exact versions
sections.what: Lists every Python package the backend needs, grouped by purpose, with an exact version for each. Running the installer on this list sets up the backend environment.
sections.why: Likely reason: exact versions keep the backend predictable across machines and over time.
sections.watch_out: Changing one version can break another package that depends on it, so test after any change.

summary: Lists the Python packages the backend needs, each pinned to one exact version.
purpose: Tells the installer exactly which library versions to install so the backend behaves the same on every machine.
why: Likely reason: pinned versions stop a library update from breaking the app without warning. The file does not say this directly.
how: The installer reads each line and installs that package at the exact version shown. Comment lines group the packages into web framework, multi-agent system, Excel export, web research and AI, utilities, and development tools.
inputs: No input data. The file is read by the Python package installer when the backend environment is set up.
outputs: A Python environment with the listed packages installed.
risks: Old pinned versions may contain known security flaws and will not get fixes unless someone updates them. Development test tools are installed along with the app packages if the whole file is installed.
debug: If installation fails, look for version conflicts among the langchain and langgraph packages. Try a fresh environment with the same Python version. Install packages one at a time to find which one fails.
